- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or shows strong downward momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.  
- If model forecast is significantly above recent 5-day average (e.g., >10% above), consider mean reversion bias; adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts sharply within 5 days, adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to reflect new sentiment direction.  
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 60% recent sentiment, 40% historical) to improve responsiveness.
